content.title: Popeyes Just Launched ONE PIECE Collab—And Fans Are Already on the Hunt for the Limited Collectibles
content.text: 3 min readThe collectibles are the main draw—and they’ll go fast: Limited drops and early social media buzz mean fans will need to act quickly.Fans were already hyping it before launch: ONE PIECE’s massive fanbase has been circulating leaks across TikTok, Reddit, and X.It’s more than a meal—it’s a viral moment: Themed items and collectibles turn this into a shareable, repeat-visit experience.Anime fans, prepare to set sail—because Popeyes just dropped its first-ever ONE PIECE collab, and this one isn’t just about the chicken. It’s about the loot—including limited-edition boxes and merch fans will have to move fast to score.(If you’re not familiar, ONE PIECE is the long-running, globally beloved anime about a crew of pirates searching for the ultimate treasure.)Toei AnimationLaunching April 13 in partnership with Toei Animation, the limited-time menu turns your usual Popeyes run into something closer to a Straw Hat crew pit stop—with exclusive collectibles designed to trigger full-on “Gotta catch them all” mode.More From Good HousekeepingSunscreen | Good to Know | Good HousekeepingLIVECurrent Time 0:00Total Duration 6:43And yes, the food is themed. But make no mistake: the real treasure here isn’t the biscuit—it’s what comes with it.This isn’t just a meal—it’s a full-on fandom dropCourtesy of PopeyesFast food collabs live and die by the extras, and Popeyes clearly understood the assignment.This ONE PIECE drop leans hard into fan-first details and collectible hype, the kind that gets posted, traded, and hunted down across TikTok and Reddit within hours. Think less “quick lunch” and more “limited-edition merch drop you can eat.”If you’ve ever wanted to eat like Luffy mid-adventure (or just justify a second visit for “collection purposes”), this is your moment.Here’s what’s on the menuCourtesy of PopeyesThe lineup is playful, themed, and very much built for the camera:Luffy Bento Bundle ($13.99): Two pieces of fried chicken, creamy mac & cheese, a Gum-Gum Fruit Lemonade, and Chopper’s CupcakeLuffy Bento Box ($7.99): Fried chicken + mac & cheeseGum-Gum Fruit Lemonade ($3.49): Bright, citrusy, and clearly designed for the ‘gramChopper’s Cupcake ($3.99): Cute, sweet, and almost too adorable to eat (almost)It’s giving Grand Line lunchbox energy—comfort food with just enough theming to make it feel like part of the adventure.Let’s be honest: No one is assembling the Straw Hat crew for mac and cheese alone.Before Popeyes even made it official, fans were already circulating TikToks, Reddit leaks, and X (Twitter) posts of the merch—because of course they were.This content is imported from x. You may be able to find the same content in another format, or you may be able to find more information, at their web site.The exclusive collectibles are what elevate this from a standard limited time offering into something fans will actively chase. Limited availability + built-in fandom = repeat visits, trading, and instant social buzz.If you want the limited-edition Bento Box, you’ll need to move fast—only select guests will score one, with more merch (think keychains and tees) dropping online April 15.Courtesy of PopeyesThis is the same playbook that made past collabs go viral—but with ONE PIECE, the stakes are higher. The fanbase is massive, loyal, and very online. If there’s something rare in the mix, expect it to disappear faster than Luffy clearing a meat platter.What’s actually worth orderingIf you’re going in with a strategy (as you should), here’s the move:Get the Luffy Bento Bundle: It’s the full experience—and your best shot at maximizing whatever collectible rollout Popeyes has in playDon’t skip the lemonade: The Gum-Gum Fruit tie-in is gimmicky in a fun way, and it’s easily the most on-theme itemChopper’s Cupcake = pure fan bait: It’s cute, it’s collectible-adjacent, and yes, people will post itTranslation: this is less about building the perfect meal and more about unlocking the full collab experience.Why anime fast food collabs keep getting biggerBetween ONE PIECE’s global dominance and the rise of fandom-driven drops, this collab hits a very specific sweet spot: food + collectibles + internet culture.Anime isn’t niche anymore—it’s mainstream, it’s global, and brands know fans will show up (and show out) when there’s something exclusive on the line. Just look at McDonald’s viral ‘WcDonald’s’ anime drop or Pokémon Happy Meals—fans will absolutely show up (and line up) when collectibles are on the table.So whether you’re here for the chicken, the cupcake, or the chance to score something rare, one thing’s clear:Popeyes didn’t just launch a meal—they launched a treasure hunt.Susan (she/her) is the recipe editor at Good Housekeeping, where she pitches ideas, parses words, and produces food content. In the Test Kitchen, she cooks (and samples!) recipes, working with developers to deliver the best written versions possible. A graduate of Brown University and a collaborator on several cookbooks, her previous experience includes stints at Food & Wine, Food Network, three meal kit companies, a wine shop in Brooklyn and Chez Panisse, the pioneering restaurant in Berkeley, California.
